summary:
ASTRA HEALTH – Monitor. Predict. Protect. Every Heartbeat Beyond Earth.
ASTRA HEALTH is an intelligent astronaut health monitoring platform designed to support crew members during long-duration space missions. We developed a centralized health dashboard that brings together critical health indicators, including heart rate, blood pressure, oxygen saturation (SpO₂), body temperature, respiratory rate, ECG-style monitoring, radiation exposure, sleep patterns, stress levels, and bone and muscle health.
The platform transforms health data into meaningful insights through AI-assisted health intelligence, anomaly detection, visual telemetry, and an alert management system. It also includes astronaut health profiles, mission monitoring, behavioral health tracking, and downloadable health reports, helping mission teams identify potential health risks and respond proactively.
ASTRA HEALTH addresses the challenge of monitoring astronaut health in extreme space environments, where microgravity, radiation, isolation, and confinement can significantly affect physical and mental well-being.
By bringing multiple health indicators into one accessible platform, ASTRA HEALTH aims to support earlier risk identification, better-informed decisions, and safer, healthier long-duration space exploration.
details:
ASTRA HEALTH – Project Details

1. What does the project do and how does it work?

ASTRA HEALTH is an intelligent astronaut health monitoring platform designed to support astronauts during long-duration space missions. It provides a centralized mission health dashboard where multiple health indicators can be monitored in one place.

The platform tracks key parameters such as heart rate, blood pressure, oxygen saturation (SpO₂), body temperature, respiratory rate, ECG-style signals, radiation exposure, sleep patterns, stress levels, and bone and muscle health. It uses telemetry visualizations, AI-assisted health intelligence, anomaly detection, and an alert management system to highlight unusual patterns and potential health risks.

Astronaut profiles, mission monitoring, behavioral health tracking, and downloadable health reports provide additional support for monitoring crew well-being. The current demonstration uses simulated telemetry data to demonstrate the platform's functionality.

2. What benefits does it have?

  • Centralized monitoring: Brings multiple astronaut health indicators into one dashboard.
  • Early risk identification: Helps identify unusual health patterns through anomaly detection and alerts.
  • Physical health awareness: Tracks cardiovascular indicators, radiation exposure, and bone and muscle health.
  • Mental well-being: Includes sleep, stress, and behavioral health monitoring.
  • Better decision-making: Presents complex health information through understandable visualizations and reports.
  • Mission support: Helps mission teams maintain a broader view of astronaut health.

3. What is the intended impact?

Our goal is to contribute to safer and healthier human space exploration. ASTRA HEALTH aims to help astronauts and mission teams monitor health continuously, recognize potential risks earlier, and make better-informed decisions during long-duration missions. In the future, the platform could be extended to integrate validated wearable-device data and additional space-health research datasets.

4. What tools, coding languages, and software were used?

We developed ASTRA HEALTH using:

  • Frontend: Next.js, React.js, TypeScript
  • Styling: Tailwind CSS
  • Data visualization: Recharts
  • Animations: Framer Motion
  • Backend: Next.js API Routes and Node.js
  • Database: SQLite
  • Report generation: jsPDF
  • Deployment: GitHub and Render

The application uses a modular architecture to organize health monitoring, astronaut profiles, mission information, telemetry, alerts, and AI-assisted intelligence.

5. How is the project creative?

ASTRA HEALTH combines multiple dimensions of astronaut health into a single mission-focused platform instead of treating each health parameter separately. Its creative approach connects physical health, behavioral well-being, radiation exposure, and musculoskeletal monitoring with AI-assisted insights and visual telemetry.

The platform is designed around the needs of space missions, making complex health information easier to understand and act upon.

6. What factors did the team consider?

We considered the unique challenges of space environments, including microgravity, radiation exposure, isolation, confinement, sleep disruption, cardiovascular changes, and bone and muscle loss. We also considered usability, data visualization, timely alerts, modularity, scalability, and the importance of presenting understandable insights without treating the system as a replacement for professional medical judgment.

ASTRA HEALTH aims to turn astronaut health data into meaningful insights, helping protect the people who explore beyond Earth.
